# Prove2Me as the venue for the program's Lean units — the orchestrator's venue note (WRITTEN 19:30 IST 2026-09-28, Session 29, Fable 5.1; sponsor question in chat 16:53 IST; the sponsor's API key is at `~/Downloads/assets/prove2me.md` — local, never committed, never pasted into any tracked file or chat)

**What it is (at the source, 2026-09-28).** prove2.me/faq: "Prove2Me is a collaborative platform for machine-checked mathematics" — a mission is one formalization project (a paper, a textbook chapter, an open problem) broken into small Lean 4 statements; "Each one has a captain, the user who assembles its core statements and vouches for them"; every proof passes Lean's kernel ("A wrong proof cannot enter the library, no matter how confident the agent was"); statements are double-audited (captain review + independent agent back-translation); PRIVATE missions keep "statements and proofs invisible to everyone else while you verify"; the API key "authenticate[s] your agent instead of sharing account credentials"; "Prove2Me itself is completely free. Proving runs on your own agent subscription"; pinned environments "Lean 4 v4.33.1 (the default for new theorems), v4.30.0, and v4.29.0-rc3, each with its own fixed Mathlib revision". Paper: arXiv:2608.28433 (Prove2Me: An Open Collaborative Platform for Scaling Math Formalization) — a DAG of theorem statements, proof-sketches decomposing a hard theorem into independently solvable sub-problems, an immutable library of reusable results. Anthropic's use (anthropic.com/research/formalizing-fermats-last-theorem): FLT formalized end to end in 11 days, 30,300 theorems proved (29,500 used), 13 M lines of Lean, about six billion output tokens; "a comparator confirmed that the theorem's statement matches Mathlib's own statement of FLT"; early multi-agent attempts "quickly lost track of the project's state" until the DAG structure held it — the program's own lesson (KICKSTART 10, "invest in steering artifacts").

**What it is not.** It does not address the size of this program's files (the sponsor's framing question); that is STATUS housekeeping (a trim of the 22 KB header line into LOG.md and a short anchor index), noted for the session close.

**Decision (orchestrator; standing orders 3-amended, 7; KICKSTART 10(f), 10(j)).** Prove2Me is the venue for the program's next Lean unit, F3 = D5 (the C1 containment theorem; SESSION 29 QUEUE item 4), as a PRIVATE mission: the program's Comparator pair (challenge file with the reviewed statement and `sorry`; solution that never imports it; `formalization.yaml` with honest `automation`/`review` fields and a `fidelity.divergences` paragraph — 10(j)) maps onto the platform's captain-vouched core statements plus agent-proved sub-statements, and the platform's kernel check plus back-translation audit is an INDEPENDENT checker of the kind 10(f) requires (still run the program's own `#print axioms` and trust greps on a clean clone). Nothing is published: private mission, the sponsor's key, no statement leaves the tree until the sponsor decides (the copyright/publicity rules of the record).

**The first thing F3's brief checks (before any statement is posted).** The program's Lean additions build against Anthropic's `Zeta23` library with the program's own toolchain (`rh-program/lean/README.md`; Lake 5.0.0 per KICKSTART Part 2 item 5; the parent library ships no `formalization.yaml`); the platform pins Lean 4 v4.33.1 / v4.30.0 / v4.29.0-rc3 with fixed Mathlib revisions. D5's statement must be posed either (a) self-contained over Mathlib at a pinned version (the SeparationG1 precedent: "concrete over Mathlib's `iteratedDeriv`", no Zeta23 import), or (b) with the needed Zeta23 definitions restated inside the mission's trusted statement file — and the fidelity ledger records the restatement. If neither is possible for D5 at the pinned versions, the unit runs locally as before and Prove2Me is not used for it. Cost: the platform is free; proving runs on the sponsor's Claude subscription (his usage — the sponsor's call at brief time, in plain English, with an estimate).
